task.description: WF-03 Step 4 rework (iteration 1 of 3): TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step-04b) found AC3's four-role InstancesAdvanceTimer matrix only had direct/indirect coverage for PROCESS_OPERATOR and TASK_WORKER -- AGENT_RUNNER and PLATFORM_ADMIN were never asserted anywhere in the diff. Add direct unit coverage for all four roles named in design doc §6 AC3.

result.summary: Added a new describe block 'ISS-0389 AC3 -- InstancesAdvanceTimer role matrix (all four named roles)' to test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs, immediately before the 'roles_from_strings/1' describe block. Four dedicated tests, matching this file's existing per-role 'grants X, denies Y' pattern (e.g. the acceptance-criterion-2 block's 'PROCESS_OPERATOR grants InstancesCancel, denies DefinitionsWrite' style): 'PROCESS_OPERATOR grants InstancesAdvanceTimer' (assert role_allows?), 'TASK_WORKER denies InstancesAdvanceTimer' (refute), 'AGENT_RUNNER denies InstancesAdvanceTimer' (refute), 'PLATFORM_ADMIN grants InstancesAdvanceTimer' (assert). All four of design AC3's named role/permission pairs are now directly, unambiguously asserted at the unit level, not merely inferred from router-level 200/403 tests. No other file touched -- the router-level PROCESS_OPERATOR/TASK_WORKER coverage from the prior iteration was left as-is since the validator judged it adequate and non-duplicative.
